current_activity: Hitzfeld takes over the new Eleventh Army on 2 April; it fights around Mühlhausen in Thuringia in early April
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 381: "the hastily constituted Eleventh Army (Hitzfield)"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 11.Armee, commanders: "General der Infanterie Otto-Maximilian Hitzfeld 2. April 1945 - 8. April 1945"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 11.Armee, text: "Anfang April 1945 geriet die 11. Armee in heftige Kämpfe im Raum Struth bei Mühlhausen in Thüringen". Event definition: the Lexikon dates Hitzfeld's command from 2 April (Lucht, named first, did not take up the post); CMH has the army under Hitzfeld in the first days of April. Event support: two source families (CMH and the Lexikon). Location: Mühlhausen, Thüringen with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: Mühlhausen stands for the area of Struth in which the Lexikon puts the army in early April; no headquarters place is named. Location support: the Lexikon names the area of Struth near Mühlhausen for the early April fighting; CMH names no headquarters place. Commander: General der Infanterie Otto-Maximilian Hitzfeld. Opponents: US Third Army.

location_qualifier: destination area of the withdrawal; headquarters place not named
current_activity: Lucht replaces Hitzfeld at the Eleventh Army on 8 April and is ordered to pull everything into the Harz
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 389: "Hitzfeld relinquished command of the Eleventh Army to General Lucht"; p. 390: "General Lucht had been in his post only a few hours on 8 April"; "all available troops were to withdraw into the Harz"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 11.Armee, commanders: "General der Artillerie Walther Lucht 8. April 1945 - Kapitulation". Event definition: the change of command and the withdrawal order on 8 April; Hitzfeld returned to the LXVII Corps. Event support: two source families (CMH and the Lexikon). Location: Harz mountains (representative point at Braunlage) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a representative point at Braunlage for the Harz mountains; the army headquarters moved from town to town and CMH names the Harz as the destination. Location support: CMH names the Harz as the area the army was ordered into; no headquarters place is given. Commander: General der Artillerie Walther Lucht. Opponents: US First Army.

source_locator: R567: p. 404, 405; R662: text of the army page
current_activity: US patrol captures the Eleventh Army staff and Lucht at the command post near Blankenburg on 23 April
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 405: "Finally, on 23 April, a patrol found the Eleventh Army command post near Blankenburg and captured the staff, including General Lucht"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 11.Armee, text: "Die Reste der Armee gerieten Ende April 1945 im Raum Blankenberg in Kriegsgefangenschaft". Event definition: the capture on 23 April; the Lexikon gives only the end of April. Event support: two source families (CMH and the Lexikon). Location: Blankenburg (Harz), Sachsen-Anhalt with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: a town point for Blankenburg; CMH says the command post was near the town. Location support: both sources put the end of the army near Blankenburg in the Harz (the Lexikon spells it Blankenberg). Commander: General der Artillerie Walther Lucht. Opponents: US 2d Armored Division, 83d Division, 1st Division.
